text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool (cobalt-pool) node n-gpu-17 entered MAINT mode due to thermal trip + unexpected PCI disconnect. Impact: several VPC tenants (including Cobalt Finance) saw request failures and fallbacks. Paging alice_oncall.

alice_oncall: I'm on it. status page? any customer pages from Cobalt?

sre_jay: I see GPU fan speeds spike, then kernel logged AER/PCIe detach. dmesg snippet: `GPU0: nvlink: link down, AER severity=corrected` followed by `nv-host: device removed`.

infra_maya: Host reported PCH thermal event at 03:21 UTC, node started kernel resets. Host agent started graceful drain at 03:22 (auto-policy). Some pods failed to evacuate quickly because CUDA processes had locked memory.

incident-bot: Automated mitigation started: attempted soft-drain -> repeated SIGTERM to processes -> escalated to SIGKILL after 30s. Drain status: 14/18 tenant allocations moved; 4 stuck (Cobalt Finance x2, internal-test).

alice_oncall: Symptoms for customer? any 5xxs in logs? Solutions team ping them?

solutions-liz: Cobalt Ops (tom@cobalt) says their in-flight requests started 500ing at ~03:20, they rolled to fallback model variant automatically. They asked to avoid eviction if possible because they were running a long batch job.

cust_ops_tom: Liz / Alice — we saw a batch job mid-run, but fallback preserved latency. We need a handoff/clear timeline for post-mortem. Currently advising retry.

alice_oncall: Ok. Two priorities: 1) isolate the faulty host and finish evacuating tenants safely (avoid data corruption for Cobalt). 2) ensure customer fallback capacity remains stable.

eng-runtime: Suggest pinning Cobalt to their reserved capacity in the same AZ to finish batch, then rehome remaining allocations off the node. We have spare reserved slots in az-east-2b.

infra_maya: I can force-evict CUDA jobs but want signoff from SRE and PMs who own customer SLAs. Forced eviction will drop in-flight state for Cobalt.

alice_oncall: Don't KILL yet. Jay, can you attempt a targeted checkpoint for the two Cobalt jobs? Are they using our managed checkpointing?

sre_jay: They use app-level checkpoint. We can attempt to send SIGUSR1 to trigger checkpoint hook. I'll run: `ssh n-gpu-17 'ps aux | grep cobalt_batch && kill -USR1 <pid>'`

(deployer-bot): Running command: `ssh n-gpu-17 'kill -USR1 4321'` -> output: `USR1 delivered to pid 4321, checkpoint started (app ack in 12s)`

alice_oncall: Good, hold on evictions for those two until checkpoint completes. Maya, continue draining other allocations.

infra_maya: Draining remaining non-blocking allocations now. k8s drain shows: `pod/tenant-x migrate -> success`, `pod/internal-test -> failed -> rescheduled`. 10/18 moved, 6 remaining (2 are the Cobalt batch ones, 4 low-priority can be force-evicted).

sre_jay: Checkpoint ack from Cobalt app: `checkpoint success, saved to /mnt/checkpoints/ckpt-2026-03-15-0324`. They requested we snapshot before kill.

alice_oncall: OK. Force-evict the 4 low-priority ones, keep Cobalt pinned and start migration to reserved slots. Eng-runtime, please allocate two reserved GPUs in az-east-2b and route Cobalt there.

eng-runtime: Allocated two reserved GPUs: reserve-az2b-004/005. Creating routing rules and updating tenant assignment. Will take ~30s.

(deployer-bot): Applied assignment update for tenant cobalt-finance -> reserve-az2b-004. Rolling start.

infra_maya: Evicting low-priority pods now: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=10 n-gpu-17` -> 4 pods terminated/rescheduled.

alice_oncall: Confirmed Cobalt job resumed on reserve nodes?

cust_ops_tom: Yes, cobalt batch resumed at 03:29 on the reserved instance. No data loss. Appreciate the checkpoint handling.

incident-bot: Node n-gpu-17 health: unreachable from BMC after kernel panic -> host flagged for manual intervention. Marking node quarantined.

infra_maya: I've set host to QUARANTINE and triggered a maintenance workflow to replace the card. Filing hardware ticket to provider with logs.

engineering runtime: Recommend we add a transient rule to route any new Cobalt allocations to reserved capacity for next 2 hours while we complete validation. Also suggest a canary run for small job to ensure perf parity.

solutions-liz: I'll coordinate customer comms: status updated to Customers -> "Partial impact: Cobalt Finance experienced transient 5xxs; batch recovered on reserved capacity. We're replacing the faulty host. No data loss reported."

alice_oncall: Handoff: I'm handing to infra_maya for hardware replace and to eng-runtime for routing policy follow-up. I'll remain in thread for post-mortem.

infra_maya: Ack. Hardware ticket created PR-4521 -> vendor RMA request, ETA parts 48-72h. Node will stay quarantined.

eng-runtime: Routing rule applied for 2h. Canary job passed at 03:45 (latency within 5% of baseline). I'll coordinate with SRE for permanent placement later.

sre_jay: Logging timeline for post-mortem: root cause: sudden PCIe detach likely due to NVLink controller thermal excursion causing device removal -> kernel teardown -> blocked drains. Mitigation: soft-drain + checkpointing + reserved rehome. Action items: 1) Investigate preemptive QoS that forces lighter weight pre-drain to reduce timeouts. 2) Improve automatic checkpoint triggers for long-running tenant jobs. 3) Add BMC liveness checks to escalate earlier.

alice_oncall: Thanks team. I'll open incident PM and include timeline and comms. Closing live paging. If any customer escalation, ping me. :thumbsup:

cust_ops_tom: Thanks everyone — will follow up for post-mortem and SLA notes.

incident-bot: Incident closed (paging cleared) by alice_oncall at 03:49 UTC."
